sources.citation: Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mebu/Ma is NOT included (only five Yupna languages were known; Mebu was added later by Z'graggen). Family-level remark p. 66 (sec. 6): 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat. In none of these languages does it carry a heavy functional load.' 'Yupna' here is the Kewieng/Yopno language (yopn1238), not Ma. Footnote 11 (p. 75) adds that for Wantoat Davis (1967) states stress is non-phonemic.

sources.note: Only one reference for the language: Z'graggen 1975 (doctype a wordlist or less; cited for subclassification, p. 9). No grammar, sketch, phonology or dictionary is known to Glottolog. Alt names Ma, Mawam, Mebu; AES 6a Vigorous (Ethnologue 2025).

sources.citation: transnewguinea.org (Greenhill) — searches for Mebu / Ma / Yupna
sources.note: No Ma/Mebu entry; Yupna entries are Bonkiman, Domung, Nankina, Yopno (Kewieng, Nokopo). Domung page sources McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 only.

sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content. Exactly three resources: Glottolog 5.2 'Resources for Ma (Papua New Guinea)' (oai:glottolog.org:mapa1244), Ethnologue 'Ma: a language of Papua New Guinea' 2018 (oai:ethnologue.com:mjn), LINGUIST List 'Resources for Ma' 2017 (oai:linguistlist.org:lang_mjn). No primary texts, lexical resources, recordings or language descriptions from PARADISEC, ELAR, Kaipuleohone, TLA, Rosetta or SIL archives.

sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content. 17th ed.: Alternate names Mawam, Mebu; population 570 (2003 SIL); Madang Province, southwest of Saidor, Mibu and Tariknan villages; 6a Vigorous; Trans-New Guinea, Finisterre-Huon, Finisterre, Yupna; 'Dialects: Mina. Related to Nankina [nnk] (Jerung)'; vigorous use, also Tok Pisin; literacy in L2 20%; Latin script. 14th ed. (2001): 'MEBU.. 319 (1981 Wurm and Hattori).. 10 to 20 miles southwest of Saidor.. Related to Yupna, Gabutamon.'

sources.citation: SIL-PNG. c. 2007-2013. PNG Language Resources: 'Language: Ma' [mjn], pnglanguages.org/pacific/png/show_lang_entry.asp?id=mjn (Internet Archive copy 2016-04-26).

sources.citation: Husa, Geoff & Shannon Husa (Ethnos360, formerly New Tribes Mission PNG; Mibu church-planting team, resident in Mibu village from March 2002). Unpublished Ma ('Mibu') language materials: practical orthography, vernacular literacy curriculum (revised 2012 with NTM literacy consultants), translated scripture portions and Bible lessons; documented only through the team's 'Mibu Ministry' blog (2007-2026) and Ethnos360 missionary page.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing linguistic is published: the blog and Ethnos360 page describe language learning, the creation of a written form ('From no written language..'), a mother-tongue literacy programme with printed curriculum materials and 'literacy boxes', and ongoing Bible translation and lesson development. Under NTM-PNG procedure an orthography presupposes an in-house phonemic analysis and culture/language file, which would be the only post-1975 first-hand description of Ma in existence; none of it is in SIL-PNG's archive (no mjn items), OLAC, Joshua Project ('No reported resources'), png.bible or any r…
